selected_candidates.title: Physics-solver MCP re-execution equivalence
selected_candidates.tightened_claim: A contracted-sandbox MCP integration makes physics-solver results re-executable under recorder-versus-replayer equivalence with per-step canonical-digest identity and an explicit determinism contract.

kill_test.named_prior: NabaOS / Tool Receipts, Not Zero-Knowledge Proofs (arXiv:2603.10060)
kill_test.assessment: NabaOS signs tool-execution receipts and independently re-fetches URLs for deep delegation; its checked abstract does not re-execute a physics solver under an explicit recorder-versus-replayer equivalence contract. The paper's current generic first wording still needs the tightened physics-solver scope before submission.

selected_candidates.title: Physics state in the full agent-loop receipt
selected_candidates.tightened_claim: Physics-solver-computed fields, geometry hashes, and world deltas are load-bearing state in a single-timestep perception-cognition-action-physics receipt chain.

kill_test.named_prior: Blockchain-monitored perception-reasoning-action pipelines and event-sourced agent runtimes

Local CAELAgent code hashes geometry plus solver field data before and after action.

selected_candidates.title: Multi-modality trait conflict algebra
selected_candidates.tightened_claim: Single-user, single-object grab/throw/hover conflicts on one transform channel are resolved with a disjoint-write distributivity side condition that separates sequential composition from conflict merge.

kill_test.named_prior: Same-author Paper 3 plus the current runtime and proof surface
kill_test.assessment: The runtime semiring resolver and commutativity tests are shipped. The paper states a disjoint-write precondition in a definition, but it does not contain the separately identified Theorem 2 and the repository has no distributivity test. Keep the contribution at deterministic multi-modality resolution until that formal/evidence gap is closed.

sources.finding: Tests commutativity against imperative last-write-wins but not distributivity.

selected_candidates.title: Receipt-backed NISQ ceiling characterization
selected_candidates.tightened_claim: A simulator-to-QPU workflow emits tamper-evident, offline-verifiable receipts that bind inputs, results, backend job identifiers, and the explicit NISQ-ceiling conclusion without claiming quantum advantage.

kill_test.named_prior: IBM Runtime job provenance, Qiskit compilation verification, and transparent VQE hardware characterization
kill_test.assessment: Job IDs, later result retrieval, compilation verification, and transparent H2/VQE hardware characterization are prior art. Keep Paper 37 as a HoloScript evidence-chain and NISQ-ceiling case study, not a first or quantum-advantage claim; its distinguishing engineering delta is the canonical offline hash joined to online job retrieval and an explicit no-advantage boundary.
